story.value: Molybdenum was discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele, a Swedish pharmacist and chemist.
The name molybdenum comes from the Greek word molybdos, which means "lead".
In ancient times, people used the word "lead" for any black mineral that leaves a mark on paper.

uses.value: Some electrical filaments are made from molybdenum.
Molybdenum is mainly used as an alloying agent in steel.
Molybdenum disulfide, a compound of molybdenum, is used as a lubricant at high temperatures.
Molybdenum trioxide, a compound of molybdenum, is used to make enamels stick to metals.
